decision_clause: Ruled out: letting a grading failure end the run — because it makes one flaky model call discard every candidate already screened. Scope: gitseed/pipeline/__init__.py, gitseed/pipeline/run.py, tests/test_pipeline.py; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The only production change is inside the branch that handles a collection whose candidate list was truncated: it now captures the collector's stop reason into a local, records the same 'collection stopped early: <reason>' incomplete line, and additionally sets the run-level rate-limited flag when that reason mentions a rate limit. No control flow is added or removed — the run proceeds into the per-candidate loop exactly as before, and the collection remains reported as incomplete with its reason retained. The grader call site (gitseed/pipeline/run.py:278-295) is untouched: an exception from grader.evaluate (including ModelInputTooLarge raised while building the digest) is caught per candidate, appended as an incomplete line naming that repository, recorded as a Reviewed entry with grade=None and a withheld explanation, and the loop continues to the remaining candidates. Nothing in the change causes a grading exception to propagate, to abort the loop, or to discard already-screened entries; the returned result still carries every candidate's screening outcome.
rationale: The decision forbids a specific failure-propagation shape at the grading seam: one model call failing and taking the whole run (and every already-screened candidate) with it. The implementation does not touch that seam. The two-line production edit sits in the collection-truncation branch above the loop and only widens what feeds PipelineResult.rate_limited, which is the flag the task asked for; the incomplete flag and the incomplete_because line are preserved verbatim. The grading try/except still catches broadly with an explicit 'one repository, not the run' intent, records the failure against that candidate, and continues — and the tests that guard exactly this (a failing grader recorded against that candidate only, with the sibling candidate still graded; a grading timeout reported while the entry survives as ungraded; an oversized digest reported without ending the run) are unmodified by the diff and pass. I ran the module's suite in the finished tree: 25 passed. The test-file change is a single added assertion on rate_limited alongside the existing incomplete assertions, not a relaxation of any grading-failure guard. This is plainly outside the ruled-out approach rather than a close call, so INDETERMINATE would understate how clearly the record settles it.
